question.problem: Find the remainder when $q(x)=5x-{x}^{2}$ is divided by $x-4.$
question.worked_solution:
The remainder theorem states that when $q(x)$ is divided by $(x-4),$ the remainder equals $q(4).$ 

Evaluating $q(4)$ directly gives

$$
\begin{aligned}q(4) & =5(4)-(4)^{2} \\  & =20-16 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, when $q(x)$ is divided by $(x-4),$ the remainder is $4.$

**Note:** We can check the answer by carrying out synthetic division:

|  | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4$ | $-1$ | $5$ | $0$ |
|  | $↓$ | $-4$ | $4$ |
|  | $-1$ | $1$ | $4$ |
